text:
jamie: Heads-up, we've got a pretty clear skew in the routing scores where low-cost regions are winning even when p95 latency is noticeably worse. Thinking out loud: we need a normalization layer so cost/latency/region/tier are comparable before scoring. any opinions on where this lives? compile-time vs runtime vs sidecar?

anish: +1 noticed this in the last canary. root cause is simple math — cost in $/token vs latency in ms. We need a consistent mapping function. Options i see: z-score per-metric, min-max with clamping, or a sigmoid mapping to damp extremes.

rachel: prefer something deterministic and cheap. do the heavy lift at compile-time: compute transforms per-model/per-region from sampled telemetry, bake coefficients into policy. runtime should only apply a small lookup + multiply. avoids per-request stats calc.

liam: counterpoint — if we do only compile-time we lose agility for live incidents (region flapping, sudden infra changes). sidecar can apply a locality multiplier learned from recent telemetry (last 5m) to adjust. tradeoff: consistency vs agility.

sana: proposal that tries to blend both: 1) compile-time baseline transforms for fairness and reproducibility, 2) sidecar runtime hints that are optional overrides with TTL and guardrails. runtime API shape proposal:

```yaml
route_descriptor:
  model: "gptx-13b"
  baseline_transforms:
    latency: {type: "percentile_map", params: {p50: 20, p95: 150}}
    cost: {type: "linear", params: {scale: 1.0}}
  runtime_hints: # optional, time-limited
    region_multiplier: {region: "us-west-2", multiplier: 1.12, expires_at: 1712340000}
    tier_boost: {tier: "dedicated", boost: 0.95}
```

sana: sidecar writes hints only if local telemetry crosses thresholds and signs them with node-id so central can audit.

anish: important to keep invariants: (a) scoring must be monotonic w.r.t inputs, (b) overrides must have bounded effect (e.g., clamp multiplier to [0.8, 1.25]), (c) we should log both pre/post-normalized scores for rollout analysis.

jamie: agree on invariants. also want to avoid adding heavy math into the hot path. runtime should be: fetch route_descriptor, apply transforms, then compute final score. if sidecar hint exists, apply after baseline but before final normalization step.

liam: operationally, how do we push new baseline transforms? rollout model: compile-time change -> canary pool -> metric checks (latency/cost/win-rate) -> global. include rollback if route-winning bias > threshold.

rachel: also add a version fingerprint for transforms so route descriptors are cache-keyed. that makes invalidation explicit. sample key: `model|transform_v|region_cohort` in our caches.

route-bot: deploy-bot: staged policy v2 applied to canary group: canary=tenants:beta, started at 7912345683 :rocket:

jamie: ok next steps: i'll draft an RFC that: (1) defines canonical transform types (percentile_map, zscore, sigmoid, linear), (2) defines compile-time bake + sidecar hint schema, (3) lists invariants + clamp ranges, (4) outlines rollout / telemetry checks. i'll ping @eng-runtime and @policy-team for review. ACTION: jamie to open PR by EOD. :thumbsup:
